summary: Oskar von Hinüber is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics scholar who studied at Tübingen, Erlangen-Nuremberg, and Mainz (Ph.D. 1960–1966 under Paul Thieme). He served at Mainz (1965–1981) and as Professor at Freiburg (1981–2006).

Osmund Bopearachchi studied at the University of Kelaniya, CNRS, Panthéon-Sorbonne (Ph.D. 1987), and Paris-Sorbonne (habilitation 1998). He served at the CNRS (Emeritus Director 1989) and as Adjunct Professor at UC Berkeley (~2014).

Osvald Sirén was a Sinology and art history scholar who completed his doctoral studies at the University of Helsinki (1897–1900). He held a professorship at Stockholm University (1908–1923) and served as Keeper at the Nationalmuseum (1926–1945).

Othmar Frank was an Indologist who studied at the universities of Paris (~1814–1817) and London (~1817–1819). He held professorships at the University of Bamberg (~1804–1807), the University of Würzburg (1821), and the University of Munich (1826).
Otoya Tanaka was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji (~1925–1929). He later served as a professor at Chuo University (~1957–1974).
Otto Blau studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1848) and the University of Leipzig (~1848–1851), studying under August Friedrich Pott.

Otto Fischer worked in Sinology, Japanology, and art history, studying at Tübingen, Munich, Vienna, and Göttingen (habilitation 1912). He served as director of the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart (1920) and professor at the University of Basel (~1927–1937).

Otto Franke was a scholar of Sinology and Indology who studied at Freiburg, Göttingen (doctorate 1884–1886), and under Wilhelm Grube. He held chairs at the Hamburgisches Kolonialinstitut (1910–1923) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1923–1931).

Otto Höfler was a linguistics and religious studies scholar who studied under Rudolf Much at Vienna (PhD 1926, habilitation 1931), Lund, and Kiel. He held professorships at Kiel (1935), Munich (1938–1945, 1954), and Vienna (1957–1971).

Otto Jahn was an archaeology and linguistics scholar who studied at Kiel, Leipzig, and Berlin. He held academic posts at Kiel (~1839–1842), Greifswald (~1842–1847), Leipzig (~1847–1851), and the University of Bonn (~1855–1869).

Otto Maenchen-Helfen worked in Sinology, archaeology, and Central Asian studies. He studied at Vienna, Gothenburg, and Leipzig under August Conrady, later holding posts at the Marx-Engels-Lenin Institute (1927–1929), Mills College (1939–1947), and UC Berkeley (1947–1962).

Otto Neugebauer was a historian of mathematics who studied at Graz, Munich, Copenhagen, and Göttingen (PhD ~1926) under Boris Turayev. He held professorships at Copenhagen (1933–1939) and Brown (1939–1969), and was a member of IAS (1945, 1969–1990).

Otto Rosenberg was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Indology. He studied at Saint Petersburg, Bonn, under Theodore Stcherbatsky and Hermann Jacobi, and held a professorship at Saint Petersburg State University from 1911 to 1919.

Otto Stein was an Indologist who earned his Dr. phil. at Charles University (1912–1918) under Moriz Winternitz and Heinrich Swoboda. He later served at Charles University as Privatdozent (1922) and ordinary professor (1930–1939).

Otto Strauss was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Munich, Berlin, and Kiel (doctoral degree ~1905) under Paul Deussen and Hermann Oldenberg, holding professorships at Calcutta (1913–1920), Kiel (1920), and Breslau (1928–1935).

Otto von Böhtlingk was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg, Berlin under Franz Bopp, and Bonn under Christian Lassen. He served at the Saint Petersburg Academy of Sciences (1842–1868) and the University of Jena (~1868–1885).

Owen Flanagan is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fordham University (~1968–1972) and Boston University (~1973–1978). He was appointed Professor of Philosophy at Duke University (~1996).

P. A. Payutto is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (-1962). He served there as Associate Dean (~1964) and was Tipitaka Acharaya at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (1995).
P. Anujan Achan worked in Indology and archaeology, studied under Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya, and served as Government Archaeologist at Thrissur Zoo and State Museum.
P. B. Meegaskumbura is an Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at the University of Ceylon, attested in 1991 and 2010.
